correctness.rationale: From Liu–Qin–Huang proved two-variable kernel formula (P e^{w·})(z)=e^{zw}V(z,w), joint exponential bound and zero-product equivalence, if all symbols nonzero then V nonzero. For m arbitrary select separated evaluation points with V(a_j,w0)≠0. A direct derivative-Cauchy bound gives Borel transforms of V(a_j,·) analytic outside bounded disks. Formal differentiation establishes B[e^{a_j·}h_j](lambda)=Bh_j(lambda−a_j); a putative linear combination vanishing implies zero on connected exterior and analytic continuation of each transform through its own disk. Entire continuation decays at infinity and is zero by Liouville, contradiction. Therefore m evaluation rows independent on image for every m; no finite positive rank. Zero factors vanish. This analytic proof is all finite product lengths and rank cutoffs, not an experiment.

originality.rationale: FAIL: the claimed zero-versus-infinite rank dichotomy is a direct mathematical corollary of the Borichev–Rozenblum 2013 general Fock finite-rank theorem (Theorem 3.1), combined with the already-established exponential-type kernel representation and inverse heat transform J_{-1} in Liu–Qin–Huang 2026. If P e^{wz}=e^{wz}V(z,w) and V is jointly entire exponential type, put A=J_{-1}V=e^{-∂_z∂_w}V, and define the smooth anti-Wick symbol F(z)=A(z, ar z). Liu–Qin–Huang Section 3 proves J_{-1} preserves E_2, so |F(z)|<=Ce^{R|z|}, hence F belongs to Borichev–Rozenblum D_{1,-}. Gaussian kernel integration or polynomial approximation yields T_F e^{wz}=e^{wz}J_1 A(z,w)=P e^{wz} on all reproducing kernels. Finite algebraic rank of P on the common invariant domain gives finite-rank kernel form for T_F; the image functions and coefficient functions are entire exponential type by linear evaluation, meeting Borichev–Rozenblum definition. Their Theorem 3.1 forces F=0, hence A=0, V=0, P=0, and the 2026 Theorem 1.2 forces one factor zero. Thus the final claim is covered by a prior stronger finite-rank theorem and established heat transform, despite an alternate Borel proof; not best-knowledge novel.
residual_risks: Primary Borichev–Rozenblum full arXiv PDF Theorem 3.1 explicitly covers Fock Toeplitz operators with D1,- symbols; the canonical anti-Wick symbol of this product belongs to its admissible class, so coverage is decisive, not just an inaccessible priority suspicion.
The alternative Borel separation proof may be a useful presentation, but no independently new mathematical theorem or claim survives as stated.
